explanation: German writes der Hund, the dog, and die Freiheit, freedom. English printers often capitalized nouns in the 1700s, and Danish did so until a spelling reform in 1948.

claims.text: Standard German spelling capitalizes all nouns.
Standard modern Dutch, Swedish and Norwegian do not capitalize every noun.
In German, der Hund means 'the dog' and die Freiheit means 'freedom', and both nouns take capitals.
English printers in the 1700s often capitalized nouns.
Danish capitalized nouns until a spelling reform in 1948.
